lines: Dr. Andrea Feinberg and Josh Hix argue that integrating nutrition into clinical practice can slash healthcare expenditures by up to two-thirds for vulnerable populations with diet-responsive chronic conditions.
The speakers highlight that severe food insecurity correlates with a 70 percent increase in annual household medical expenditures, making nutritional intervention a powerful lever for cost reduction.

Scaling food-as-medicine models requires shifting the industry focus from forced behavioral modifications to removing friction in access, despite current barriers such as a lack of nutritional education in medical training.
The guests note that utilizing existing digital infrastructure and consumer touchpoints can drastically improve patient compliance compared to traditional pharmaceutical treatments.
title: Replay: On Food as Medicine (2020)
